chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad al-Basri, from Abu Dawud al-Mustaraqqy, from one who narrated it to him, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He called for dates, ate them, and then proceeded to drink water after them. So I said to him: 'May I be your ransom! If only you would refrain from the water.' He said: 'I eat the dates precisely so that I may find the water pleasant afterward.'

key_terms.تَمْر: Dates (dried fruit of the date palm) — a highly recommended food in Islamic tradition
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be your ransom — a reverent expression of devotion used toward Imams
key_terms.لِأَسْتَطِيبَ: So that I may find pleasant/aromatic — the Imam ate dates to enhance the taste of water

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq eat dates before drinking water?
ai.summary: A companion narrates being present with Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) and observing him eat dates followed by drinking water. When the companion suggested the Imam refrain from water, the Imam explained that he intentionally ate the dates in order to enhance the pleasantness and taste of the water afterward. This narration reflects the Imam's attention to the pleasures and blessings of lawful food and water, illustrating a Prophetic tradition of appreciating the goodness of simple sustenance.
word_analysis: so that I may find pleasant
